questions.question: Which language is known as ‘Italian of the East’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Telugu**__

 
• **Telugu** is often referred to as the 'Italian of the East'.
 
• The phrase highlights the melodious and rhythmic quality of the Telugu language, which is reminiscent of the Italian language's musicality.
 
• Telugu is a Dravidian language spoken predominantly in the Indian states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
 
• It is one of the twenty-two scheduled languages of the Republic of India and is also a classical language of India.
 
• Telugu has a rich literary tradition and has produced many notable works in literature, poetry, and drama.

 
• **Kannada** is another Dravidian language spoken predominantly in the state of Karnataka.
 
• **Malayalam** is the principal language of the Indian state of Kerala and the union territories of Lakshadweep and Puducherry.
 
• **Marathi** is an Indo-Aryan language spoken predominantly by people of Maharashtra.
 
• Each of these languages has its own unique linguistic features and cultural significance.
 
• The term 'Italian of the East' specifically refers to the lyrical and rhythmic qualities of the Telugu language.

questions.question: ‘Kalamezhuthu' is a ritual art form found in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘Kalamezhuthu' is a ritual art form found in Kerala**__.

 __
 
• Kalam (Kalamezhuthu) is a **unique form of this art** found in Kerala.

 
 
• It is** essentially a ritualistic ******art****** practised in temples** and **sacred groves** of Kerala where the **representation of deities like Kali and Lord Ayyappa**, are **made on the floor.**
 
 
 
• Kalamezhuthu is a ritual art form of Kerala wherein the deity’s form is drawn on the **floor using five types of coloured powders.**
 
• This is practised by many communities in Kerala and is a part of many ritual forms.
 
• Kalamezhuthu and Pattu are conducted to **propitiate the deities and to avoid untoward happenings.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalamezhuthu:**

 
 
• It is practised during festivals in **Bhadrakali **(Mother Goddess) temples, and on special occasions in** SarppaKavu **(groves sacred to snakes) and** AyyappanKavu** (temples dedicated to Lord Ayyappa).
 
• Various deities are** picturised using coloured **powders.
 
• Kalamezhuthu is done by various communities such as** Kaniyan, Vannan, Puluvar, Malayan, Pulayar, Maavilar, Munnoottan, Parayan, Paniyan, Aaviyar, Velan, Mannan, Koppaalan, Kuravar, Theeyaattunni, Theeyadi Nambiar, Theyyampadi Nambiar, Varanattu Kuruppanmar, Kallatta Kuruppanmar, Puthusseri Kuruppanmar, Marar** and so on.

questions.question: Which of the following musical instruments is an example of the stringed instruments played by the Manganiars of west Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Kamaicha.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kamaicha:**

 
 
• It is a bowed lute played by the** Manganiars of west Rajasthan.**
 
• The whole instrument is one piece of wood, the spherical bowl extending into a neck and fingerboard; the resonator is covered with leather and the upper portion with wood.
 
• There are** four main strings and a number of subsidiary ones passing over a thin bridge**.
 
• It links the sub-continent to** Western Asia and Africa** and is considered by some scholars to be the oldest instrument, with the exception of the** Ravana Hatta or Ravana Hasta Veena.**

questions.question: In which of the following place, are the Dilwara temples of Jainism located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mount Abu**__.

**Dilwara temples of Jainism located at Mount Abu.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dilwara Jain Temples** is one of the finest Jain temples known in world for its **extraordinary architecture and marvelous marble stone carvings **and are located at **Mount Abu.**
 
• These temples were built between the **11th to 13th Centuries AD.**
 
• All this was done at a time when no transport or roads were available at a height of 1200+ Mtrs in Mount Abu. 
 
• Huge blocks of marble stones were transported on elephant backs from the Arasoori Hills at Ambaji to this remote hilly region of Mount Abu. 
 
• Dilwara temples are also a popular **Jain pilgrimage attraction**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Dilwara Temple complex consists of** five major sections or temples devoted to five Jain Tirthankaras (Saints)**:

 
 
• Shri Mahaveer Swami Temple 
 
• Shri AdiNath Temple or Vimal Vasahi Temple
 
• Shri ParshavNath Temple or Khartar Vasahi Temple
 
• Shri Rishabdaoji Temple or Peethalhar Temple 
 
• Shri NemiNathJi Temple or Luna Vasahi Temple

questions.question: 'Lai-Phi’ and ‘Chin-Phi’ are the cultural costumes of which state?

__
 
• **Lai-Phi** and **Chin-Phi** are traditional cultural costumes of the state of **Manipur**.
 
• These costumes are often worn during festivals, cultural events, and traditional ceremonies in Manipur.
 
• The attire reflects the rich cultural heritage and craftsmanship of the Manipuri people.
 
• Manipur, located in the northeastern part of India, is known for its diverse culture and traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Manipur's capital city is **Imphal**, and the state is often referred to as the "Jewel of India" due to its scenic beauty and rich culture.
 
• The people of Manipur celebrate several festivals such as **Yaoshang, Lai Haraoba, Ningol Chakouba, and Kang**.
 
• Manipur is also famous for its traditional sports like **Polo** and the indigenous game of **Thang-Ta**.

questions.question: With which of the following communities is the word 'Langar' (community kitchen) mainly associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikhism**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **Langar** is primarily associated with **Sikhism**.
 
• Langar, meaning community kitchen, is a practice in Sikhism where free meals are served to all visitors, regardless of their background, religion, or social status.
 
• This tradition was initiated by Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism, and has been continued by his followers to promote equality and service to humanity.
 
• Langar is typically found in Gurdwaras (Sikh temples) worldwide and is an essential aspect of Sikh community life.
 
• The food served in Langar is vegetarian to ensure that it is acceptable to people of all dietary preferences.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sikhism** was founded in the 15th century in the Punjab region of India.
 
• The **Gurdwara** is a place of worship for Sikhs, where the Guru Granth Sahib (holy scripture) is read, and Langar is served.
 
• The principles of Sikhism emphasize **selfless service, equality, and community welfare**.
 
• Langar exemplifies these values by providing food to anyone in need, fostering a spirit of community and inclusiveness.
 
• Other religious traditions also have similar practices of community kitchens, but the term Langar is most closely linked with Sikhism.

questions.question: Who among the following was NOT a Nayanar saint?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Nayanars and Alvars were the Tamil poet-saints who played a key role in propagating the Bhakti Movement in Southern India during the 5th-10th Centuries.
 
 
• The Nayanars were a group of 63 saints devoted to Lord Shiva who lived during the 6th to 8th centuries CE.
 
• The Alwars were Tamil poet-saints of South India who espoused devotion to the Lord Vishnu or his avatar Lord Krishna in their songs of longing, and service. 
 
• **The names of the Nayanars were first compiled by Sundarar.**
 
• When we study the lives of the great Four Teachers (**Appar, Sundarar, Manickavachagar, and Sambandar**__) and realize that these great Jnanis, too, were great Bhaktas who loved to visit the temples and sing the glories of the Lord.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **​Sundarar :**

 
 
• **Sundarar means "the lovely, handsome one".**
 
• Sundarar (Murthi) Nayanar flourished in the 8th century.
 
• He was a great devotee of Lord Siva.
 
• He is one of the Tamil Samaya Acharyas (four Tamil religious Teachers).
 
• Sundarar (Murthi) Nayanar was born in Thiru Navalur where the entire atmosphere was full of spiritual vibrations and Saivism was well established.
 
 
 
• **Sambandar: **
 
 
• He was a Saiva poet-saint of Tamil Nadu who lived sometime in the 7th century CE.
 
• He is one of the most prominent of the sixty-three Nayanars, Tamil Saiva bhakti saints who lived between the sixth and the tenth centuries CE.
 
• He was a contemporary of Appar, another Saiva poet-saint.

questions.question: Which of the following is a limestone cave in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Borra Caves**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Borra Caves are located on the East Coast of India, in the Ananthagiri hills of the Araku Valley of the Alluri Sitharama Raju district in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Borra Caves were formed as a result of the flow of the Gosthani River on the limestone deposits.
 
• The cave is a unique gift of nature. The cave is deep, nearly 400 steps down and up.
 
• Borra Caves are deemed to be among the largest in the country and are perched at a whopping elevation of about 705 metres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Undavalli Caves**, a monolithic example of Indian rock-cut architecture and one of the finest testimonials to ancient Viswakarma sthapathis, are located in Mangalagiri Tadepalle Municipal Corporation of Guntur district in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh
 
• **Varaha Cave **Temple is a rock-cut cave temple located at Mamallapuram, on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal in Kancheepuram District in Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• **The Bhimbetka **rock shelters are an archaeological site in central India that spans the Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods, as well as the historic period.

questions.question: Dogri language is mainly spoken in which of the following states/union territories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jammu and Kashmir.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dogri** language, member of the Indo-Aryan group within the Indo-European languages.
 
• Dogri is spoken by approximately 2.3 million people, most commonly in the Indian state of **Jammu and Kashmir.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dogri **was added by the 92nd Amendment Act of the Constitution of India, officially known as The Constitution (Ninety-second Amendment) Act, 2003.
 
• The act amended the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution so as to include Bodo,** Dogri**, Maithili, and Santali (Santhali) languages, thereby raising the total number of languages listed in the schedule to 22.
 
• Ram Nath Shastri was born on 15 April 1914. He is known as the "Father of Dogri" for his pivotal role in the revival and resurgence of the Dogri language in Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.question: 'Rahide' is a long scarf worn by the women of ______ to protect their head from cool breeze as well as to show their traditional social affinity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Himachal Pradesh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rahide**__

 __
 
• **Rahide is a long headscarf worn by the women of Himachal Pradesh to protect their heads from the cool breeze and also to depict their tradition.**
 
• **Rahide** comes in different fabrics and patterns. The most commonly used pattern is the **floral print that denoted the rich flora and fauna of the state and its surroundings.**
 
• These scarves have been made mostly by **local women for centuries.**
